Where it began

Tamim Iqbal was born in the port city of Chittagong on 20 March 1989, into a family steeped in the game. His brother Nafees Iqbal and his uncle Akram Khan both played Test cricket for Bangladesh. Even so, Nafees was happy to say that Tamim had the greater gift.

Tamim played at the Under-19 World Cup in Sri Lanka in 2006, and a year later he was at the senior World Cup. In his first big moment, against India in the group stage, he made a brisk 51 from 53 balls and helped his side to victory.

The player

He played 70 Tests between 2008 and 2023 and made 5,134 runs at 38.89, with 10 hundreds, 31 fifties and a top score of 206.

His maiden Test hundred came in the West Indies in July 2009. His 128 set up Bangladesh's first Test win over the West Indies, their first win overseas, and soon afterwards their first series victory away from home. In 2010 he made a hundred in each Test of a short tour of England, and Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year and its Test Player of the Year. In 2017 he became the first Bangladeshi to reach 10,000 international runs, and he went on to make 25 international hundreds, more than any of his countrymen.

What made him special

He was at his best when he went after the bowling. At the 2016 World Twenty20 he hit more sixes than anyone and made more runs than anyone, including his country's first T20 international century. He was also the only Bangladeshi with a hundred in all three international formats.

In one-day cricket he was a rock for over a decade. In 2020, with Litton Das, he put on 292 for the first wicket against Zimbabwe, a Bangladesh record for any wicket. He also led the one-day side in 37 matches and won 21.

County cricket was a quieter chapter. A short stint with Nottinghamshire in 2011, only the second by a Bangladeshi, brought 104 runs in five matches, and he judged it fairly himself: it could have been better, but it was not too bad.

Away from the middle

He turned out in Twenty20 leagues from Pakistan to the Caribbean. In domestic cricket he made 334 not out for East Zone, the highest first-class score by a Bangladeshi. In 2024 he captained Fortune Barishal to their first Bangladesh Premier League title. In June 2026 he was elected president of the Bangladesh Cricket Board.

And finally

By 2018 he had made more one-day runs at Colombo's R. Premadasa Stadium than anyone had ever made at a single ground. Not bad for a ground in another country.
